texts.preamble: Da vs Kishan Dutt Sharma & Another on 16 May, 2019 In The Court Of Ms. Gurmohina Kaur, Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate - 01 Patiala House Courts, New Delhi Cc No. 56582/16 Date of Institution : 23.11.2009 Date of reserving judgement : 16.04.2019 Date of pronouncement : 16.05.2019 In re: Delhi Administration / Food Inspector Department of Pfa, Govt. of Nct of Delhi A-20, Lawrence Road Industrial Area, Delhi-110035 ... Complainant Versus 1. Sh. Kishan Dutt Sharma S/o. Sh. Amar Singh, M/s Bengali Sweet House, 27-34, Bengali Market, New Delhi-110001 R/o. Village & P.O. Manana, Distt. Panipat, Haryana. 2. M/ s. Bengali Sweet House, 27-34, Bengali Market, New Delhi-110001. ..... Accused persons Judgment
texts.facts: 1. The present is a complaint filed under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 ( PFA Act), wherein it is alleged that the accused persons had sold misbranded food in violation of Section 2(ix)(k) of PFA Act read with Rule 32 (a)(b)(c) (e) and partial violation of Rule 32(f) and violation of Rule 32(i) and 36(2)(a) of PFA Rules, 1955 punishable under section 16(1) DA vs Kishan Dutt Sharma & another (a) of PFA Act. 2. As per the complaint, on 04.04.2008 at about 6.00 pm, the food officials including Food Inspector (FI) Suniti Kumar Gupta and Field Assistant (FA) Ashok Kumar under the supervision of Local Health Authority (LHA)/ SDM Sh. M.S. Vats reached at the premises of M/s Bengali Sweet House, 27-34, Bengali Market, New Delhi-110001. The accused Kishan Dutt Sharma was found Da vs Kishan Dutt Sharma & Another on 16 May, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52493213/ 1 vending the business of various food articles, including Mogra Namkin which were found stored for sale of human consumption , lying in sealed packets of 200 gms, each bearing identical label declaration. The food officials lifted the sample of the said food article consisting of 6 sealed packets of Mogra Namkin ready for sale. It was divided into three parts as per procedure prescribed under the PFA Act and Rules and separately packed and sealed. Necessary documents were prepared at the spot including the vendor's receipt and panchanama. Price of the sample was paid to the vendor. One counterpart of the sample was deposited with the Public Analyst(PA) and remaining two counterparts were deposited with SDM/LHA. Vide report date 30.04.2008, the PA reported that the article was conforming to the standards, yet the sample was found misbranded being in violation of Rule 32 a,b,c,e, partial violation of Rule 32f and violation of Rule 32(i) and 36(2)(a) of PFA Rules. Based on the report of PA, investigation was carried out by the Food Inspector as per the instructions of the SDM/LHA. It was found that Accused No. 1 Kishan Dutt Sharma was the vendor of M/s Bengali Sweet House, 27-34, Bengali Market, New Delhi-110001 at the time of taking samples. Accused No. 2 M/s Bengali Sweet House was a partnership firm DA vs Kishan Dutt Sharma & another and it had appointed accused No. 1 Kishan Dutt Sharma as its Nominee under the provisions of PFA Act and Rules and he was incharge of and responsible for day to day conduct of the business of the said firm being a partnership firm Accused No. 1 Bengali Sweet House was also liable. The sampled article of food "Mogra Namkin" was manufactured by the firm/accused No. 2 M/s. Bengali Sweet House itself. After obtaining due sanction of the Director, PFA, the present complaint came to be filed against the accused for violation of the section 2(ix)(k) read with Rule 32 (a)(b)(c)(e), partial violation of Rule 32(f) and violation of Rule 32(i) and 36(2)(a) of PFA Rules, 1955 as punishable under section 7/16(1)(a) of PFA Act for selling misbranded food. 3. Since the complaint was filed by a public servant in writing, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the accused was summoned vide order dated 30.09.2010. Based on the report of PA, notice of accusation u/s 251 Cr.PC was framed vide order dated 15.04.2011 against the accused persons for commission of offence under Section 7/16 (1)(a) of PFA Act for violation of provisions of Section 2 (ix)(k) of PFA Act,1954 along with Rule 32 and 36 of PFA Rules, 1955. 4. At the trial, the prosecution examined four witnesses in support of its case, PW-1 FI Sh. Suniti Kumar Gupta, PW3 Sh. M.S.Vats SDM/LHA and PW4 Sh. Ashok Kumar was part of the team that had visited the premises of accused persons and lifted the sample of Mogra Namkin lying in sealed packets of 200 gms each. PW2 FI N.N. Sharma also IO in the present case. These witnesses deposed about the sample proceedings conducted by DA vs Kishan Dutt Sharma & another them on 04.04.2008 and narrated the steps undertaken by them, including disclosing their identity, lifting 6 sealed packets of 200 gms each, dividing the same in three counterparts by considering one sealed packets as one counterpart and separately packing them. A sum of 168/- was paid to the vendor as price of the sample vide vendor's receipt Ex. PW1 / A. Vendor issued cash memo Ex.PW1/A-1. Notice in form VI Ex.PW1/B and Panchanama Ex. PW1/C were prepared on the spot. Raid Report is Ex.PW1/D. One counterpart was deposited with the PA vide receipt Ex.PW1/E and remaining two counterparts were deposited with SDM/LHA vide receipt Ex.PW1/F on the next working day. PA report Ex. PW1/G was received opining the sample to be misbranded. Further investigation was Da vs Kishan Dutt Sharma & Another on 16 May, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52493213/ 2 carried out during which letters Ex.PW-1/H was written to STO and reply Ex.PW1/H-1 was received that M/s. Bengali Sweet House was a partnership firm. Letter sent to Chief Health Officer, NDMC was Ex.PW1/I and letters sent to vendor were Ex.PW1/J and Ex.PW1/J-1. Request for information from PFA Department was Ex.PW1/K wherein reply was received that the nominee of M/s. Bengali Sweet House was Albert James Dass and in his absence, Kishan Dutt Sharma shall be responsible during the time of his duties as 'alternate nominee'. Letter received from M/s. Bengali Sweet House was Ex.PW1/L wherein it was mentioned that Kishan Dutt Sharma continued to be the nominee of the firm despite the death of one of the partners and that his continuation was with his consent. Letter received from accused Kishan Dutt Sharma was Ex.PW1/M wherein he stated that he was person in charge of and responsible for day to day conduct of the business of the firm, including the day of sampling. Letters sent to VAT Officer, Ward DA vs Kishan Dutt Sharma & another No. 7 were Ex.PW1/N and Ex.PW1/N-1. Thereafter, investigation was marked to PW2. The consent for prosecution was obtained Ex.PW2/A from Director, PFA. After which complaint Ex.PW2/B was filed before this Court and intimation letter Ex.PW2/C alongwith postal receipts Ex.PW2/D was sent to the accused persons. These witnesses were cross-examined by Ld. Counsels for accused persons. 5. PW1 denied the suggestion that he did not make any effort to join any public witness. He also denied the suggestion that the 6 packets of Mogra Namkin which he took as sample were not yet ready for sale. PW1 also added that he did not inquire from the Department regarding the first violation by the Firm as the policy of issuing warning of first violation under Rule 32 of PFA Rules had been already withdrawn on the date of sample proceedings. PW3 admitted during his cross-examination that the sample was lifted to analyse the same for adulteration and added that whenever a sample was sent for analysis, it was also ascertained if the sample complied with PFA Rules and was misbranded or not. He also stated that the packets were suitable containers and admitted that the contents on the same were not complete and therefore was in violation of PFA Rules. He admitted that removable stickers bearing such information was in violation of Rules. 6. Statement of the accused persons were recorded under section 313 Cr.PC on 25.04.2017 wherein they denied the allegations and pleaded innocence. Accused No. 1 admitted the sample proceedings. Accused No. 1 and 2 opted to lead Defence DA vs Kishan Dutt Sharma & another evidence. 7. Accused No.1 Kishan Dutt Sharma examined himself as DW1 and stated that he was working as a Nominee with M/s. Bengali Sweet House, Bengali Market, New Delhi and on 04.04.2008 a raiding party consisting of three persons including SDM, FA Ashok Kumar and FI Suniti Kumar came at the shop and showed their intention to purchase the sample and FI Suniti Kumar took 6 packets of 200 gm each of Mogra Namkin as a sample and he added that FI did not accept any request and forcibly took the sample and made three counterparts of two packets each and further added that the sample of Mogra Namkin was however declared as per standard. During his cross-examination by Ld. SPP for complainant, he did not make any complaint in the PFA Department regarding this fact.
texts.arguments: 8. It is in these circumstances, Ld. SPP for the complainant has argued that the complainant has been able to prove its case against the accused beyond reasonable doubt, as both the witnesses have supported its case and there is no contradiction in their testimony. It is submitted that the accused Da vs Kishan Dutt Sharma & Another on 16 May, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52493213/ 3 persons have failed to rebut the findings as given in the PA Report. 9. On the other hand, Ld. Defence Counsel for the accused No.1 and 2 have argued that accused No. 1 and 2 were falsely implicated and that the sticker on the sample food article was yet to be affixed. He has also argued that Accused No. 1 Kishan Dutt Sharma had no role in the present case. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Shriram Labhaya v. MCD [1948-1997 FAC (SC) 483] has categorically held that testimony of the Food Inspector alone, if believed, is sufficient to convict the accused and there is no requirement of independent corroboration by public persons unless the testimony suffers from fatal inconsistencies.
